prompt:
You receive 4 images. Image 1 is the LAYOUT SKETCH of the finished 1920x1080 game screen: a crude flat-colour blocking that fixes the exact composition - camera, horizon, wall and floor lines, and the position, size and outline of every object. Repaint image 1 into a finished painting: keep every line and every block exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is, paint each block as the object described below, do not move, enlarge, shrink, add or remove anything, and leave no flat colour areas or hard geometric edges. Images 2-3 are photos of the real place (geography, architecture, materials and real details to paint from; they are references only, do not copy their camera, cars, people, signs or weather). Image 4 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: the inside of grandmother Mira's old garden outbuilding behind her house in the old village core of Čierna Voda (municipality Chorvátsky Grob, near Bratislava, Slovakia). Image 2 is a real old Central-European home workshop in such an outbuilding: rough lime-plastered brick walls, a worn workbench with an iron vice, old tins, an old leather bag, tools on nails - paint the walls, materials and age from it. Image 3 is our own finished painting of this property seen from the street (the small red-brick workshop with the plank door, the green picket fence, the yellow grapevine with dark grapes, the pale peach and light blue house): what is seen through the open door must match it. An invented interior, not a copy of the photo; leave out every brand, label and plastic chair of the photo.

Brief: the entrance room of a separate, uninhabited garden outbuilding with its own outer door: old suitcases, a shelf of old school teaching aids, a brass instrument case on a shelf, and an open doorway to a further workshop room behind. A quiet, dusty, slightly mysterious but homely storeroom of a grandmother who used to be a teacher. A sunny autumn afternoon on 29 October 2020: warm low sunlight falls in through the open door on the left and draws a bright patch on the floorboards; dust motes in the light; the rest of the room in soft warm shade. Same light and palette as image 4.

Camera: exactly as frontal and flat as image 4 - eye level, looking straight at ONE wall. The back wall is parallel to the picture and fills the picture from the left edge to the right edge; no side walls, no room corners, no walls or beams running into the depth; the ceiling beam runs horizontally across the top of the picture. Keep this exact geometry from the sketch: the ceiling and beam at y 0-76, the high shelf board at y 252, the top of the shelving unit at y 252, the window at y 150-380, the skirting where the wall meets the floor at y 780 across the whole width, and the floorboards from y 792 to the bottom edge.

What the sketch blocks are: at the top old dark timber ceiling boards and one heavy timber beam across the room; the back wall is rough whitewashed lime plaster over brick, with a patch of bare red brick top right and a damp stain; at the far left (x 0-118) a narrow strip of the open outer doorway in this same back wall, cut by the left picture edge, with a wooden jamb, full of bright autumn daylight, showing Mira's garden exactly as in image 3 - yellow vine leaves with dark grapes, the green picket fence, a sunlit garden path; a short high wooden wall shelf on black iron brackets at the left; under it a low old wooden chest of drawers standing flat against the wall, with a few old unlabelled tins and an old brown leather doctor's bag on top of it; a ski pole leaning on the wall; a tall old wooden shelving unit standing flat against the wall, full of old school teaching aids - old textbooks, a wooden abacus with coloured beads, a box of wooden geometric solids, white plaster cone and sphere models, an old brass microscope, stacks of old exercise books, rolled school wall maps lying on the lowest shelf, a big wooden blackboard triangle and compass; nothing but the globe stands on top of it; a bare light bulb hanging from the beam (off); a small dusty four-pane window glowing with the yellow autumn garden outside, with a sill; three old suitcases stacked on the floor under the window (big brown leather, cardboard, small green); an old bow saw and a coil of wire on nails and an old metal watering can on the right; at the right an open doorway without a door, under a timber lintel, into the darker back workshop room, where a faint soft blue glow comes from a round light on the far wall. The wall meets the floor at y 780 along the whole width.

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. the block of the layout sketch at x 120-240, y 150-250 of the 1920x1080 frame (6-12 % from the left, 14-23 % from the top): on the high shelf, a closed old brass instrument case the size of a small lunch box, with a leather carrying handle on top, a small engraved bell emblem on the lid and a clasp that hangs open; an old tin box beside it.
2. the block of the layout sketch at x 425-545, y 150-250 of the 1920x1080 frame (22-28 % from the left, 14-23 % from the top): the curled-up tips of three old wooden skis (varnished red-brown wood, old cable bindings lower down) that stand upright side by side, leaning against the wall; the skis reach down to the floor at the wall foot.
3. the block of the layout sketch at x 730-850, y 150-250 of the 1920x1080 frame (38-44 % from the left, 14-23 % from the top): an old school globe (blue oceans, green and ochre continents, no lettering) with a brass meridian arc on a wooden foot, standing alone on top of the tall shelving unit.

Walkable floor: the band at x 90-1830, y 790-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (5-95 % from the left, 73-94 % from the top) is the worn wide pine floorboards running left to right - one continuous floor, nothing stands or lies on it: no boxes, no tools, no rugs, no cables, no buckets. Only the patch of sunlight from the door, soft shadows and a little dust. The floor continues to the left edge into the light of the outer door (the area of the layout sketch at x 50-105, y 975-1045 of the 1920x1080 frame (3-5 % from the left, 90-97 % from the top)) and to the right edge, where the open doorway leads into the back room (the area of the layout sketch at x 1870-1925, y 975-1045 of the 1920x1080 frame (97-100 % from the left, 90-97 % from the top)).
This room has no NPC zones.

Fiction rules: Mira's outbuilding is invented. No brand names, logos or readable labels on tins, boxes, books, maps, suitcases or anything else; the wall maps and book spines show no readable words or digits. No people, no animals, no 2020 gadgets.

The layout sketch is a blocking aid only: paint over all of it. Do NOT draw frames, borders, outlines or boxes around objects, and keep no flat colour block. The finished picture contains no UI, no captions, no text except what is asked for above, no watermark and no people or animals unless stated above.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
